headline: Indian Markets End Mixed as IT Weakness Offsets Banking Gains
why: Weakness in IT and Tata group stocks dragged the Sensex lower.
US Fed rate hike concerns and global sanctions created market caution.
Uncertainty around global oil tariffs following US sanctions on Russia buyers.
Banking sector showed resilience backed by positive analyst ratings on HDFC Bank.
whatHappening: Sensex and Nifty closed mixed amid Fed rate hike news and NSE IPO buzz.
UBS retained a Buy rating on HDFC Bank with a target price of Rs 1,000.
Paytm and major banking stocks remained in key focus for day traders.
Banks offered revised senior citizen FD rates up to 8.5% in September.

summary:
Indian markets traded mixed as weakness in IT and Tata group stocks weighed on the benchmark indices.
Positive sentiments in the banking sector, led by UBS's bullish stance on HDFC Bank, helped restrict losses.
Global macro factors including US Fed rate hikes and crude oil sanctions kept investors cautious.
